title: Jensen Huang Said to Have Had Relationship With Nvidia Executive Who Reports to Him
partialText: Mr. Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive, is already facing scrutiny over an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who U.S. intelligence determined was a Chinese spy.

title: Court Rules That Sexual Harassment Case Against SpaceX Can Proceed
partialText: The company had argued that the case, involving eight former workers, must be resolved before an arbitrator.

title: Trump Officials Clashed Over Megaspeed, Firm at Heart of Nvidia Affair
partialText: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confronted Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick last week about why the administration had not put restrictions on advanced chip sales to Megaspeed.

title: Silicon Valley Tech Allies Support Jensen Huang
partialText: Elon Musk and other Silicon Valley figures cast the Nvidia chief’s relationship with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy as a personal lapse, not a security failure.

title: Nvidia Scandal Puts Lori Huang, Jensen Huang’s Wife, In the Spotlight
partialText: Lori Huang, who has been married to the Nvidia chief executive for more than 40 years, stands out among tech titan spouses for how private she has been.

title: Anthropic’s I.P.O. and the Clubby Business of A.I.
partialText: Some of the biggest investors in the artificial intelligence giant’s upcoming listing are also some of its most important business partners.

title: How GLP-1 Drugs and a Revamp Revived Ro’s Business
partialText: The telehealth company said that its annualized revenue had grown nearly tenfold since it revamped its business and embraced weight-loss treatments.

title: The Fed Has to Raise Rates. How Fast to Go Has Officials Divided.
partialText: The Federal Reserve’s gradual approach to raising rates is being tested by intensifying price pressures.

title: Heating Costs Will Rise 7% on Average This Winter
partialText: People who use heating oil will see increases of around 70 percent because the war in Iran has greatly reduced supply of that fuel.

title: This Trader Raised Alarm About Nvidia’s China Entanglements Months Ago
partialText: Christian Lamarco, a 31-year-old short seller and trader, warned about financial and personal problems at Nvidia in May.

title: $150 for a Thanksgiving Pie? A Humble Dessert Staple Gets Pricey.
partialText: This season, bakers are charging three figures for luxury versions that combine elaborate prep and premium ingredients. Not everyone is biting.

title: Entertainment 360 Acquires Brigade, a Management Firm Rich in Substackers
partialText: With the purchase of Brigade, a small talent firm, Substack writers and podcast hosts are now managed by the same company as movie stars.

title: Hospitals Brace for Medicaid Work Rules and Deep Funding Cuts
partialText: Health systems are racing to guide millions of patients through new eligibility hoops, slated to go into effect Jan. 1.

title: The United States Is Skipping COP31 in Turkey
partialText: President Trump refused to send an American delegation to the United Nations climate summit in Turkey.

title: How a Suspected Chinese Spy Gained Access to Nvidia Chips
partialText: A woman whom U.S. intelligence identified as a Chinese spy had ties to Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, dating to at least 2023. Ana Swanson, our reporter on trade and economics, explains what new photos show.

title: Toyota Plans to Sell a Kei Pickup Truck in the U.S.
partialText: The automaker plans to sell Americans “Kei” pickup trucks, which are very popular in Japan and with U.S. auto enthusiasts. Even President Trump is a fan.

title: Anthropic’s Giant IPO Will Tie It Closer to Nvidia
partialText: Nvidia planned to invest $10 billion in Anthropic alongside its initial public offering, the largest of the new financial commitments from several giants to the A.I. company.

title: Nvidia Hires Wachtell Lipton to Investigate CEO Jensen Huang’s Affair With Chinese Executive
partialText: Wachtell partner Joon H. Kim, a former acting U.S. attorney, is leading the inquiry into the chip maker’s chief executive.

title: Weil Gotshal Partners Vote to Shut Down After Nearly a Century
partialText: The large law firm, known for its powerful bankruptcy practice, started coming apart as prominent partners moved to other firms.

title: Who Is Alice Huang, the Woman in the Middle of Nvidia’s Spy Scandal?
partialText: Alice Huang, who U.S. intelligence determined is a Chinese asset, emerged from the high-flying world of Shanghai finance to work with tech titans and obtain essential A.I. chips.

title: Data Show Households Still Managing to Meet Their Monthly Debts
partialText: The New York Fed detailed general steadiness in debt payments for autos, student loans and mortgages.

title: Here’s the latest.
Failure of California Billionaire Tax Strikes Blow to Progressive Agenda
partialText: A wealth tax on billionaires seemed like a political layup. The outcome of a California ballot initiative shows otherwise.

title: Nvidia’s Game of Thrones
partialText: Analysts and investors are asking whether the chipmaker needs to consider a successor to Jensen Huang, its C.E.O., as the company is engulfed in a spy scandal.

title: Anthropic Targets Valuation of Up to $1.4 Trillion for Blockbuster I.P.O.
partialText: The A.I. company’s pricing would make it one of the biggest ever public listings. It comes at a volatile moment in markets, with investors questioning the sustainability of the A.I. boom.

title: Secrets, Chips and Spycraft: The Nvidia C.E.O. Scandal
partialText: Despite knowing about the relationship between one of the president’s closest allies and a woman later identified by U.S. officials as a Chinese spy, the Trump administration took no action.

title: Here’s why last year’s government shutdown will haunt October’s inflation data.
Elevated Inflation Keeps Pressure on Fed to Raise Rates
partialText: October’s Consumer Price Index report showed a broadening of price pressures that has stoked concerns about the Federal Reserve’s grip on inflation.

title: Why U.S. Business Deals Are Unlikely to Get Putin to Give Any Ground
partialText: President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia has shown a willingness to endure a high price to get what he wants in Ukraine, and he sees little reason to stop fighting now, analysts say.

title: A Fan-Favorite Aquarium Screen Saver Is Leaving Roku
partialText: The Aquatic Life display, a welcome moment of Zen in the frenzied world of TV streaming, will go dark on Dec. 1 after its designer pulled the license.

title: Advent Calendars Go Beyond Chocolate, From Pickles to Protein Powder
partialText: Snacks, drinks and health foods are helping fuel a $2.6 billion industry that serves up a treat a day, from cheese to booze to dog biscuits.

title: Haaretz Expands US Presence Amid Israel’s Move to the Right
partialText: Haaretz has more than doubled the size of its American bureau, including hiring correspondents to cover beats like national politics and young American Jews.

title: Justice Dept. Accuses Lyft of Disability Discrimination in Lawsuit
partialText: The department said Lyft and its drivers routinely deny rides to people who use stowable wheelchairs or travel with service animals. Lyft disputed the allegations.

title: ‘We Used to Be a Wealthy City’: Auto Woes Slam German Towns
partialText: The downturn in the automotive industry has done away with services and benefits that residents of Friedrichshafen, a lakeside city, once enjoyed.

title: China’s Trade Surplus Passes $1 Trillion at Record Pace
partialText: China’s factories are finding eager buyers worldwide, but the export boom is raising concerns about its impact on trading partner nations.

title: Exxon Strikes Preliminary Deal to Return to Venezuela
partialText: The agreement brings the biggest U.S. oil company a step closer to pumping oil again in Venezuela, nearly two decades after it left the country.

title: Lawsuit Says Republican Strategist Alex Bruesewitz Took Money From Qatari Interests
partialText: The suit claims that any payments to Alex Bruesewitz, a Republican strategist, could have violated federal law. He has denied ever taking such funds.

title: Boeing Will Cut 5% of Commercial Plane Employees
partialText: The company said it needed fewer workers because production was increasing more slowly than previously expected.

title: Could the Voter Backlash Against A.I. Actually Help the Economy?
partialText: Voter backlash could threaten the data center boom. Some economists think that could be a good thing.

title: U.S. Commerce Dept. Inquiry Into Megaspeed Was Halted After Nvidia Intervention
partialText: An investigation into Megaspeed, a Singapore company that was buying advanced Nvidia A.I. chips, was transferred to the Justice Department after a top Nvidia executive reached out to Commerce Department officials.

title: Oil Prices Have Tumbled in November. Here’s Why.
partialText: The global benchmark price is down more than $20 a barrel since late October, when it traded for around $113.

title: Giant Merger of NextEra and Dominion Could Fail Amid Anger Over Electricity Bills
partialText: State leaders and residents in Virginia have opposed NextEra’s acquisition of Dominion Energy, fearing that it will accelerate rate increases.

title: How Indispensable Is Jensen Huang?
partialText: The fate of Nvidia’s chief executive, who was romantically involved with a suspected Chinese spy, has wide implications for Silicon Valley, Washington and beyond.

title: China Rejects Espionage Claims Involving Nvidia C.E.O. Jensen Huang
partialText: The controversy has intensified scrutiny of Mr. Huang’s ties to Beijing and sparked mixed reactions across Asia, where he is widely popular.

title: Nvidia’s Stock Price Drops After Investigation Into CEO Jensen Huang
partialText: The chip maker’s shares fell sharply after its C.E.O., Jensen Huang, admitted to a relationship with a businesswoman suspected of spying for China.

title: Senator Tells Google to Let Schools Disable A.I. Features in Search
partialText: The request came from Senator Edward J. Markey of Massachusetts, after Google said it would not turn off artificial intelligence tools for students using its search engine.

title: A Country’s President Led to a Bank’s Stunning Rise, and Its Fall
partialText: Prosecutors accused President Santiago Peña of Paraguay of funneling nearly a billion dollars of government funds to the Ueno bank as its executives made reckless insider loans.

title: A.I.-Generated Celebrity Ads Get an Assist From Terry Crews
partialText: The Ogilvy ad agency and the CAA talent agency introduced a partnership to create promotions featuring digital replicas of celebrities.
